requirement:
Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for
Ollama. A configured value MUST override the default for either backend; zero
MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.

Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
rationale:
One obligation is unmarked and untested: retrying transient provider failures inside the affected assessment. The rest of the requirement is implemented and tested.

**Obligations and where they are met**
- **Optional positive integer `concurrency` per named config.** `AuthoringConfig.concurrency: Option<NonZeroUsize>` (src/config.rs) accepts it. Zero, negative, fractional and string values are rejected, because `UserConfig::parse` and `WorkspaceConfig::parse` decode into that type. `authoring_concurrency_defaults_overrides_and_invalid_values` and `workspace_configurations_accept_validate_and_override_concurrency` (tests/configuration.rs) test this.
- **Defaults.** `effective_concurrency` (src/config.rs) uses available parallelism, falling back to 1, for Bedrock and uses 1 for Ollama. A configured value overrides the default. The tests above cover both backends, and `ollama_batches_are_serial_by_default` checks a peak of 1.
- **Async tasks on a fixed worker pool.** `main` builds `tokio::runtime::Runtime::new()` and `author_all_with_options` spawns a `JoinSet` of async tasks. The code has no conditionals of its own, and the batch tests exercise it.
- **Running assessments never exceed the concurrency.** The launch loop in `author_all_with_options` stops at `tasks.len() < concurrency`. `batch_fills_evidence…` asserts `peak == 2` and checks that the first two requests overlapped.
- **Each assessment keeps its own conversation and usage record.** `prepare_assessment` starts its own `UsageLog` per subject. The batch tests assert one usage record per assessment (6 records).
- **Any other provider error uses the ordinary failure path.** `prepare_assessment` records the usage outcome `failed` and returns the error. `author_all_with_options` then adds it to `outcome.failures`. `failed_assessment_keeps_other_results_and_reports_failure` (HTTP 400 for one subject) tests this.

**Gap: transient failures retried within the affected assessment**
- The concurrency text requires transient failures, including throttling, to be retried within the affected assessment.
- The code that does this is `converse` in src/authoring/mod.rs. It keeps a per-conversation `ProviderBackoff` and sleeps with the async `tokio::time::sleep`. That decides the retry within the assessment's own task, without blocking a pool worker.
- `converse` carries `{impl}` for `provider_backoff` and many other requirements, but not for `requirements.authoring.concurrency`.
- No test marked `{test}` for `concurrency` covers it. The retry tests in src/authoring/mod.rs are marked only for `provider_backoff` and `usage_requests`, and they run a single assessment.
- No batch test with concurrency greater than 1 has one assessment hit a transient failure and retry while the others proceed. A search of tests/ for 429, Retry-After and ThrottlingException found nothing.
- This obligation of the subject therefore has code with no `{impl}` reference to the subject and no `{test}` for it.

No `{fixme}` acknowledges this gap, so the determination is false.

text: :::{req} concurrency
Each named authoring configuration MUST accept an optional positive integer
`concurrency` in its configuration table. When omitted, the maximum number of
simultaneous assessments MUST default to the number of available logical CPUs
for Bedrock, falling back to one when that count is unavailable, and to one for
Ollama. A configured value MUST override the default for either backend; zero
MUST be rejected as invalid configuration.
Batch authoring MUST use asynchronous tasks on a runtime with a fixed worker
thread pool. The number of assessments running at once MUST NOT exceed the
selected concurrency. Each assessment MUST retain its own model conversation and
usage record. Transient provider failures, including throttling, MUST be
retried within the affected assessment under
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider_backoff`; every other provider error MUST
be reported through the ordinary assessment-failure path.
:::{req} provider_backoff
When a provider reports a transient failure, the harness MUST wait and retry
the same completion request. Transient failures are throttling, reported
through HTTP 429 or a Bedrock `ThrottlingException`; temporary unavailability,
reported through HTTP 500, 502, 503, or 504 or a Bedrock
`ServiceUnavailableException`, `InternalServerException`, or
`ModelNotReadyException`; and a request with no response after ten minutes,
which the harness MUST abandon. The retry MUST retain its prompt, history,
tools, and pending inputs. It MUST NOT
restart the assessment or repeat already completed tool calls. A permanent
input/context-length error, authentication failure, or invalid request MUST
remain an error; mentioning tokens in an error message alone MUST NOT trigger
retries.
The backoff window MUST start at one second and double after each consecutive
transient failure, up to sixty seconds. Each delay MUST be randomly selected
between half and all of that window to spread parallel retries. An available
provider `Retry-After` value, in seconds or HTTP-date form, MUST be honored as a
minimum delay even when longer than the window. A successful response MUST reset
backoff for the next completion request. There MUST be no retry-attempt limit;
interruption MUST cancel both the wait and further retries.
Each attempt MUST be recorded under {cite}`requirements.authoring.usage_requests`.
Hidden SDK retries MUST remain disabled so the harness can account for attempts.
Transient retries MUST NOT be reported as finished judgments or terminal
assessment errors while recovery is still in progress. Pending inputs MUST be
recorded as evidence only after the request succeeds.
{cite}`requirements.authoring.provider` {cite}`requirements.authoring.delivered_inputs`
